PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

THE LAST NINE. 9 -> 0, and web has no service left that returns an object literal.

The shape half of the service rule -- a service hands back an instance, not a literal -- is closed for web: connection_recovery (71 lines behind
a closure), bottom_sheet (34), dismiss_alert (25), form_dialog_stack (25),
effect (24), popover (19), user_invite (19), demo_data (14) and http (3) each
became a class whose instance start() hands back. Nothing about what the
services do changed; what changed is that a downstream addon patching one of
them now writes one method against a prototype and composes through super,
instead of re-running the whole start() body and mutating what came back.

The conversion is not free and the bill came from ONE shape, not nine:
`makePopover` takes the add function as a parameter, and two call sites handed
it a bare `popoverService.add`. A closure service does not notice -- `add` was
a closure that had captured everything -- but a prototype method called with
no receiver has no `this`. One of the two was production code
(datetime_picker_service.js), which every datetime picker in the client goes
through, and it cost 3 popover_hook tests and 63 datetime ones before the two
sites were changed to pass a lambda that keeps the receiver. Anything else in
the fork that detaches a service method will fail the same way and just as
loudly.

Measured in a detached worktree at HEAD with only these files copied in, the
shared working tree being unusable for a count (several other sessions are
holding web/model, web/fields, web/components and mail).

Verification: web JS suite 15949 passed; the previously-failing suites re-run
together give 2 failed / 1376 passed, both command_service overlayModifier
tests that fail identically with these files reverted. eslint and tsc both
character-identical before and after.
